fields.summary: For Indian students weighing German university options, public universities charge €0 tuition and enroll 90% of students, while private institutions charge €10,000 to €20,000 yearly.
Written for Indian applicants evaluating an Ablehnungsbescheid; explains how to challenge credit or prerequisite evaluation errors via a formal Widerspruch filed within 30 days.
A guide for Indian students arriving on a Subtype D visa to convert their entry sticker into a 2-year electronic residence permit (eAT) at the local Ausländerbehörde and set up a Girokonto.
Navigates the 5-stage German immigration path for Indian families, covering Section 16b student visas, 140 full work days, the 18-month job seeker visa, and EU Blue Card transitions.
Covers the RWTHonline portal for Indian engineering applicants, detailing RWTH Aachen's €0 tuition policy and strict mandatory GRE cutoffs (75th percentile Quant) for MS Computer Science.
Explains major funding options for Indian Master's students in Germany, including DAAD scholarships, political foundation stipends (€992 monthly), and the merit-based Deutschlandstipendium.
Prepares Indian scholarship applicants for 20- to 30-minute DAAD and university selection panel interviews, focusing on defending research proposals and career goals before academic evaluators.
Guides Indian applicants on structuring technical, academic SOPs focused on curriculum modules and thesis projects alongside European tabular Europass CVs for German university admissions.
Details the TestAS aptitude exam for Indian applicants to German universities, explaining its lifetime score validity, 110-minute Core Test, and subject-specific modules offered in English or German.

Profiles 15 leading German public universities for Indian students, comparing TU9 research institutions with universities of applied sciences across tuition fees, living costs, and application portals.

Breaks down the 2-year expenses for Indian families funding a Master's degree in Germany, showing how tuition-free public universities keep total living and blocked-account costs around ₹22.5 to ₹25 Lakhs.
Explains TUM's 100-point Master's Aptitude Assessment (EFV) for Indian STEM applicants, detailing Stage 1 grade and ECTS scoring alongside Stage 2 written entrance exams for scores between 50 and 69.
Step-by-step guide for Indian students applying to TUM Munich via TUMonline, highlighting the mandatory Uni-Assist VPD certificate requirement and the strict May 31st Winter application deadline.

Walks Indian applicants through Uni-Assist degree evaluation, explaining the difference between standard submissions and VPD certificates alongside application fees (€75 first university, €30 each extra).
Provides a walkthrough of the my.uni-assist.de portal for Indian students, covering account setup, single-vault PDF document uploads (max 10 MB), application fee payments, and status tracking.

A directory overview helping Indian students filter over 400 German institutions, contrasting tuition-free TU9 research universities and applied sciences institutions against fee-charging private colleges.

Explains VFS Global booking mechanics for Indian students applying for a Subtype D visa, highlighting strict consular jurisdiction rules and the mandatory Consular Services Portal reference code requirement.

Checklist for Indian students attending VFS Germany visa appointments, detailing the mandatory two-set physical folder layout (originals and photocopies), unstapled stacking order, and Videx form requirements.
Focuses on German student visa interviews for Indian applicants, outlining consular questions on course curriculum, document alignment, and proving €11,904 funding without mentioning part-time jobs.
Outlines the German immigration timeline for Indian students, detailing Section 16b study visas, 140-day Werkstudent work rights, the 18-month job seeker permit, and fast-track PR.

Compares Winter and Summer semester intakes for Indian graduates, highlighting application deadlines (July 15 vs. January 15) and noting that Winter hosts 85% of English-taught Master's courses in Germany.
